name: Architectural, Residential and Cultural Complex of the Radziwill Family at Nesvizh
description: In central Belarus, the Radziwill family's seat at Nesvizh centres on a castle of ten linked buildings arranged around a six-sided courtyard, beside the Corpus Christi church where family members were buried. The dynasty held the estate from the 16th century until 1939. After repeated sackings and years of neglect, the castle was heavily restored between 2004 and 2012, and its design influenced architecture across Central Europe and Russia.
